Most remarkably, the company delivers an extraordinary return on equity of 60.67% against a sector benchmark of only 6.84% [E8]. This combination of a tiny ₹ 14.4 Cr market capitalization [E2] and deeply discounted book value [E1] creates a compelling valuation entry point for asset-focused investors. The business is structurally unprofitable, generating a price-to-earnings ratio of -4.63x that contrasts starkly with the sector benchmark of 25.83x [E5]. Consequently, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00%, ensuring no cash returns are distributed to shareholders while these operational deficits persist [E3].

Conceded: [E3], [E11], [E24], [E25], [E26], and [E27]. Despite those persistent negative profitability and return metrics, the bear focuses exclusively on historical challenges while ignoring the striking current valuation disconnect [E1]. The market capitalisation sits at a modest ₹ 14.4 Cr [E2], and the shares trade at an extreme discount with a price-to-book ratio of 0.28x from filed statements [E1], or 0.27x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.3x [E6]. This massive asset discount provides an immense margin of safety that more than compensates for the negative P/E of -4.63x [E5] and sub-zero ROA [E7]. Furthermore, the data provider records a standout positive ROE of 60.67% against a sector benchmark of 6.84% [E8], which completely contradicts the narrative of unmitigated operational destruction and highlights untapped earnings power at current depressed prices.

Conceded: [E8]. The bull relies on this single metric while ignoring a decade of chronic destruction, evidenced by a 10-year median return on equity of -20% [E24], a 5-year median of -21% [E25], and a 3-year median of -18% [E26]. The low price-to-book ratio of 0.28x [E1] or 0.27x [E6] is not an "immense margin of safety" as claimed, but a rational reflection of negative ROCE of -4.5% [E11], sub-zero ROA of -1.22% [E7], and an unviable P/E of -4.63x [E5] compared to the sector benchmark of 25.83x [E5].
